title: Outstanding little pump at fair price/switch is questionable
text:
UPDATE: April 2016 -- I've been using this pump for a little over a year and the pump, itself, continues to function well but I'm beginning to have problems with the float switch. The switch now turns the pump on in the full off position but, if I raise it I/2 inch, it turns off. It will restart gain at about 1 1/2 inches up or floating. I've managed to keep it working by holding it above the full off position with a rope but I'm now concerned that the rope will float away and the pump will run until it burns up or destroys the battery by running it until it is totally discharged. It appears to find a quality float switch, I'll have to spend about as much for the switch as I have for the switch and pump combo and the add-on pump. I'm still very pleased with the pump. It does what it's supposed to and does it well.

This is a strong pump for its small size and low cost. It took about fifteen minutes to pump out a twelve foot Portabote that was three quarters full of water and it's worked without fail since I installed it to keep the boat rain water free. At just over $20 for the pump and switch with an additional backup pump as a $5 add-on, this is a super bargain. So far both pump and switch have proven to be reliable but they're not designed for heavy duty use and I would not think of using them in situations where the vessel will be unattended for a long period of time or when large volumes of water need to be dealt with. While the pump can clear a significant amount of water quickly, it's really designed for light incidental use. I'm very happy with this purchase because I believe that I'm using the pump and switch as they were intended...in a non-critical situation to handle incidental rainwater and spray. To ask them to do much more could be asking for trouble.

title: High Adrenaline Thriller with quirks
text:
Music Notes is Manning Wolfe's second installation in the Texas Lady Lawyer series. It's a fast-paced, intense thriller with an eclectic cast, one of those stories that will keep you up so late at night you'll need extra coffee in the morning. Merit Bridges, the perky but powerful protagonist and her quirky team of paralegals find themselves, yet again, in opposition to a deliciously delusional villain intent on their demise.
When the rehabilitated rock guitar hero, Liam Nolan, is brutally murdered with his own guitar, Merit is not only responsible for his estate but feels morally obligated to help solve the crime. Enter Davey Ray Bell who claims to be Liam's love child. Though Davey seems lost and alone there may be some validity to his claim. Meanwhile, Liam's former manager, L A Baron, hopes to grab all the glory and the cash. When he fails to convince the legal authorities of his claim to the riches, he uses his vast resources to attempt to destroy Merit's career and reputation.
The writing is very visual and personal. Wolfe's characters are complex and for the most part driven by more than just material gain. Though the story is definitely dark, it's handled with a quirky humor and panache that brings this storyteller to the pinnacle of legal thriller authors. As an extra bonus, it's set in Austin Texas where the old hippie culture still clashes with the techno-boom of the early 21st century. Wolfe's Texas Lady Lawyer stories scream to be made into a Showtime summer miniseries featuring Reese Witherspoon and her ponytail as the protagonist. Check your local listings, but as always read the book first.

The dartboard itself is also decent; the sisal is tight, the numbers are clear, and it feels like it will hold up to a lot of play over the next few years.

However, the darts included with the set are a complete disappointment. I understand that this is a budget-friendly bundle, but these darts are almost unusable. The tips are inconsistent, and the flights are made of a cheap plastic that curls or tears after just a few throws. More importantly, the balance is completely off. I found myself struggling to hit basic targets, not because of my skill, but because the darts wobble mid-air. They feel lightweight and cheap, almost like toys you would find in a carnival game rather than actual sporting equipment.

If you are buying this for a game room or a garage, be prepared to spend an extra twenty or thirty dollars immediately to buy a proper set of brass or tungsten darts. I ended up using an old set I had in the attic, and the difference in performance was night and day.

In short, the hardware is great, but the accessories are garbage. I am giving this three stars because the cabinet and board are high quality enough to justify the price, but the inclusion of such poor-quality darts is a major letdown. It is a good foundation for a home setup, but do not rely on the darts that come in the box. Buy the set for the board, and buy your darts elsewhere.

title: This is an important book
text: First of all, I should say that I spent the last 12 years of my career working at a hospital as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, so when I received this book as a present from a friend I was excited to read it. However, after reading it, I was mystified by some of the critical reviews I found on Amazon. As an RT I spent a lot of time with patients who had breathing problems. This included patients with COPD/emphysema and asthma who struggled to breathe. The standard treatment for these conditions is a class of drugs called bronchodilators. Inhaling these drugs can save people who are unable to breathe, but especially the more chronic patients often don't respond as their bodies seem to become immune to the effects of the drugs over time. With these patients, I would often teach them some of the breathing techniques described in this book. Often I had great success in calming these patients (they're panicked because their damaged lungs make it difficult for them to breathe) and getting them to slow down their respiratory rate. I also worked in cardiopulmonary rehab with both patients who were recovering from heart attacks and pulmonary patients. When we exercised I noticed that most of them had forgotten about their diaphragms and were unable to isolated this critical pulmonary muscle during exercise. Mr. Nestor discusses this in the book. By the way, subsequent research based on the Framingham study does correlate decreased Vital Capacity (total lung volume) with increased cardiovascular risk. In any case, this book does not purport to be a medical textbook and many of the stories are anecdotal and not supported by volumes of medical double-blind studies, but I don't believe that it was the author's intent to propose breathing techniques as a way to cure diseases like scoliosis or ADHD, or as some sort of panacea for curing all illness. In fact, in the Epilogue he says this. But the book is a fascinating journey through 10+ years of the author's research into a much ignored topic. I believe that we can all benefit from practicing the techniques in this book. In short, I like his advice on the "perfect breath": Breathe in through your nose for about 5.5 seconds, then exhale for 5.5 seconds. Practice this for a few minutes. To your health!

title: Great sprinkler for little kids!
text:
I bought this sprinkler for my three-year-old and five-year-old, and it has been an absolute lifesaver during this heatwave. We have tried a few different water toys over the last couple of summers, but most of them are either too aggressive with the water pressure or too complicated to set up. This one is perfect for little kids who are still getting used to the feeling of water spraying on them.

The setup was incredibly simple. I just hooked it up to our standard garden hose, turned on the water, and it was ready to go in less than two minutes. One thing I really appreciate is that the water pressure is gentle. My youngest can run right through the middle of it without getting overwhelmed or scared, which was a big concern for us with our previous sprinkler. It creates a fun, misty environment that keeps them cool without soaking them so instantly that they freeze up.

The build quality is surprisingly durable. My kids are not exactly gentle with their toys, and they have spent hours jumping and sliding around it, but it has held up perfectly. The material feels thick and sturdy, and we haven't noticed any leaks at the hose connection, which is usually where these things fail. It is also very easy to deflate and store away when we aren't using it, so it doesn't take up much room in the garage.

What I love most is how much active play it encourages. Instead of just sitting in a plastic pool, my kids are running, jumping, and chasing each other through the water. It keeps them physically active and completely entertained for long stretches of time. It is rare to find a toy that both children are equally obsessed with, but this has become the highlight of their day.

If you have toddlers or young children and you are looking for a way to keep them cool in the backyard without any stress, I highly recommend this. It is affordable, safe, and provides hours of entertainment. It is exactly what we were looking for to make our summer more enjoyable. I am very happy with this purchase.

title: Great fragrance!  Horrible shampoo!
text:
I really wanted to love this shampoo because the scent is absolutely incredible. As soon as you open the bottle, it smells like a high-end luxury spa. It has these beautiful, sophisticated notes that linger in the air and make the actual process of washing your hair feel like a treat. If I were rating this based on fragrance alone, it would be a five-star product without question. Unfortunately, a shampoo needs to actually function as a cleanser and conditioner, and this one fails miserably in that department.

The first thing I noticed was the texture. It is far too thin, almost watery, which meant I had to use twice as much as usual just to get it to lather. Even then, the lather was weak and didn't feel like it was actually lifting any oil or buildup from my scalp. After rinsing, my hair felt strangely tacky, as if there was a film left behind that wouldn't wash away.

The real disaster happened once my hair dried. I have medium-textured hair that is usually manageable, but after using this, my strands felt like straw. It stripped every bit of moisture from my hair, leaving it frizzy, tangled, and completely lifeless. I spent twenty minutes trying to brush through the knots, and I genuinely feared I was going to cause breakage. It felt as though the chemicals used to create that amazing scent completely overwhelmed the moisturizing ingredients, or perhaps there weren't any moisturizing ingredients to begin with.

I tried using a deep conditioner afterward to save my hair, but the damage was already done. My scalp also felt itchy and tight for a few hours after the wash, which makes me suspect that the fragrance is too strong or the formula is too harsh for sensitive skin.

It is such a shame because I love the way it smells, and I almost considered using it as a body wash just to keep the scent around, but for the price point, I expect a hair product to actually improve the condition of my hair. I cannot recommend this to anyone who cares about the health of their locks. Save your money and buy a shampoo that prioritizes hair care over perfume. It is a lovely scent, but a horrible shampoo.

title: Be careful what you ask for
text:
I got this book because I heard the author and her husband interviewed recently on NPR. Based on that, I thought "Wondering Who You Are" would be a uniquely uplifting story. I expected something along the lines of Jill Bolte Taylor's "My Stroke of Insight," which was a fascinating and inspiring first-hand account of a young woman's stroke and rehabilitation. For sure, this book did keep me on the edge of my seat - I couldn't put it down (as other reviewers have noted). And it did have some engaging parts, like the description of Richard's chaotic hospitalization, the couple's experience with a mediator over the legal settlement, and Lea's sexual exploration, among others. But I came away from the book feeling it was over-wrought and just plain sad. Here is a woman (the author) who actually leads a rich, surprising, adventure-filled life, but she just can't stop weeping over her lack of self-fulfillment. It's ironic that she spends so much of the book bemoaning the loss of her remarkable husband's pre-surgery personality, and yet while she had him that way, she was an alcoholic who preferred to be out partying rather than staying home with him and her children! Clearly she is transformed by her experience with him after he loses his personality, but she seems to find barely an ounce of delight in any of his rehabilitation successes or her own exploration of the wondrous possibilities life has to offer. Instead we hear too many times about her tears.

If nothing else, what this book teaches is - be careful what you ask for. If you long for unconditional love and acceptance, here is post-surgery Richard, able to offer these things in spades…. but it's creepy. Gurus like Byron Katie teach us the joy of living in the moment and questioning our personal narratives, but those approaches to self-transformation are only viable if we have a memory and a life story - as Richard does not.

text: This cage is bigger than I thought, and is perfect for my indian ringneck parakeet! She loves it! I would not put a bird with feet smaller than an indian ringneck's in this cage,  as a smaller bird will not be able to climb the walls in this cage. King's cages are well-known for being top-of-the-line and well-built, and this cage lives up to that expectation.  I purchased the white version that has the 5/8" bar spacing (it is also available with 1" bar spacing), it arrived by frieght delivery in pieces in two boxes on a pallet and was very well-packed, so I was able to pre-schedule the delivery date. title: Taking it to the Next Level
text:
I first got this book from the library. I can honestly say, it wasn't what I was looking for at the time. As a new home brewer, I wanted to brew and drink drinkable beers as soon as I could. I have yet to meet a home brewer who has the necessary patience to make truly great brews right out of the gate. Not to say they aren't completely drinkable, just really following someone else's lead.

Half a year later I gave this book a second shot after reading "Brew Like a Monk". Reading it a second time was like two different books! What had happened?!? Well, obviously the book hadn't changed. My outlook on brewing had. It had matured and I had moved to a level of wanting to produce not only original, but consistent and delicious brews.

My first go-around I was essentially looking for shortcuts and recipes, therefore I was disappointed.

My second go-around I was really looking to understand what I was doing and wanting to control the process instead of just following a bunch of steps.

If all you want from home brewing is to brew good drinkable beer, save your money and put it towards ingredients or supplies. If you want to move your brewing and understanding of brewing to the next level in a very readable form, this book will be a good investment.

title: Mann's ambitious retelling of the Faust legend
text: Thomas Mann poured his considerable knowledge of music into this biography of fictional German composer Adrian Leverkuhn, whose musical career spans the first thirty years of the 20th century. The result is one of literature's most ambitious attempts to portray the art of music in words. At the same time, this is a self-portrait of the narrator. Writing from the perspective of 1944, like Mann himself he is a representative of an older, humanistic Germany, who looks on appalled as the Red Army marches ever closer to the German border. Hating the Nazi regime, he struggles with the fact of the national catastrophe that looms ever closer. The result is perhaps Mann's most complex novel, ironies within ironies, all contained in the story of an artist who makes a pact with the Devil (or does he? or does he imagine that he did?) in order to achieve transcendence in his art. The language is thick, the narrative moves slowly, sometimes at a snail's pace, but the complexity of the story offers rich rewards. Not for the faint of heart.

title: It can't 'bump' automatically when the water is boiled, ...
text:
I bought this kettle because it looked sleek and the price was reasonable, but it has been a bit disappointing in practice. The build quality is decent enough and it heats the water quickly, which is the main job of any kettle. However, the functionality isn't as intuitive as I expected based on the description.

The biggest issue is that it can't bump automatically when the water is boiled. I was expecting a clear signal or an automatic shut-off that I could hear from the other room, but it just stays there. I have actually forgotten about it a couple of times, leading to the water boiling away for too long. It requires a lot more attention than my previous model, which makes it less convenient for a busy morning routine.

On the positive side, the pour is smooth and it doesn't drip, which is a nice touch. The exterior stays relatively cool to the touch, so I don't have to worry about burning my hand when grabbing the handle. It works, but it lacks the basic smart features that make a kitchen appliance truly useful. If you are someone who stays right in the kitchen while making tea, this is fine, but if you need something that alerts you or shuts down reliably without supervision, look elsewhere. It is just an average product.

title: Secret Blade Kubotan ~ very cool
text:
Hey there's not a lot of things you can get for less than 3 bucks these days that will make you think, "cool!" but this little keychain kubotan made me think just that. It's small enough to not be too much of a bother on your actual key ring, but it's big enough to be used as an effective blunt kubotan self defense weapon. But wait, there's more! If you somehow manage to unscrew the bottom cap, spin it around and screw it back on, you have a deadly puncture device that can do some real damage. I say "somehow manage" because I don't think if you found yourself in a dire situation, confronted by someone meaning to do you bodily harm, that you would have the time, steady hand, or patience to get the knife out in time unless you saw the person coming from quite a way off. You need to unscrew the end cap, spin it around and screw it back in with the blade out. It's a neat way to carry a concealed blade but I don't know how it'd fare trying to assemble it in practical application.

The blade itself is not exactly a double-edged knife so much as a thick, very sharply-pointed puncturing device that will leave a hole rather than a slit. If you do manage to stick someone with this thing it'd leave them reeling in pain no matter where you hit. And like I said, blade out or not, it works great as a fist reinforcing kubotan, plus you can use the blunt end to gouge into someone's hand, face, etc. and get them to take a step back so you can make your getaway. It's solid stainless steel and for 3 bucks, it's fully functional. Be careful!

title: Excellent account of the "Emergency"
text:
I served in the army in Malaya in 1957-58, and found this book to be an excellent "refresher course" when writing my own stories for my family; we have long-standing connections with Malaya, from before WWII until just after Merdeka, and I was able to fill in some gaps and correct some errors.

I've deducted one star because of two problems: first, it is in serious need of an index, and second, there isn't much coverage of the later stages just before Merdeka (August 1957) - perhaps the CTs were effectively beaten by then, but we felt (perhaps mistakenly) that Malaya was still definitely a war zone. I suppose that when you are in the jungle and your rations are being parachuted in you get a distorted view of history!

This book dates from 1971, so naturally does not have some of the information that later writers have been able to find as records are released. I recommend Margaret Shennan's biography of John Davis, "Our Man in Malaya" (2007), as an excellent addition to the field. But of course F. Spencer Chapman's classic, "The Jungle is Neutral", is required reading for anyone trying to understand what jungle warfare really feels like.

It is rare to find a company that actually stands behind its warranty and values the customer's time.

I am giving this four stars instead of five because a product shouldn't fail within thirty days, regardless of how good the support is. text:
2/20/22 update: Today I needed to replace two cartridges, so I used two that had been provided to me by the vendor after my initial 1-star review of this product in which I noted that the cartridges were not compatible with my HP printer. The replacement cartridges worked just fine, so I have updated my review to 5-stars. Kudos to the vendor for addressing my issue. Please read below for prior reviews and additional background.

2/8/22 update: Within a day of my leaving the 1-star review, below, the vendor contacted me offering a /replacement or a refund. They said that their cartridges had "gone through a upgrade just because of t/he firmware update". That statement was not totally clear to me, but I took it to mean that the printers had a firmware update and that they had upgraded these cartridges so that they'd be compatible. I appreciated the offer of replacement or refund since I was out of the return period, and decided to give them another chance. So....I took the replacement which arrived today (only 3 days after they initially contacted me). My printer is not currently in need of any cartridges, but when it is, I will try the replacements and update my review accordingly. In the meantime, I've upgraded my review from 1 start to 3, for their attempt to make it right. Can't give a higher rating until I confirm whether the cartridges work.

Original Review: Even though the product description listed my HP printer as one that these cartridges would work in, and even though they appeared to be a match and were easy to install in the printer, they were not compatible. The printer indicated it had detected a non-HP chip, and the cartridge was blocked. This prevented the printer from doing any printing/copying. Unfortunately, since I buy my cartridges in advance, so that I'm never caught without ink, by the time I discovered this issue, I was beyond the refund period, so I had to eat the $70+ cost (including tax). I was pretty surprised by this....these cartridges had good ratings, and I ALWAYS buy off-brand cartridges and I rarely have problems. Maybe I just got a bad batch, but figured I should post this review just in case it's becoming a trend for these.

I bought this book after feeling completely overwhelmed by the stresses of my daily life and a constant cycle of anxiety about the future. For years, I felt like my emotions were driving me rather than the other way around. While that sounds basic, the way the author explains how to detach from the ego and stop the internal noise is life-changing. I found the practical exercises incredibly helpful. Instead of getting swept away by a wave of anger or sadness, I now have a toolkit to observe those emotions without becoming them. It has given me a sense of peace that I didn't think was possible.

My relationships have improved because I am more present during conversations and less reactive during conflicts. I feel more centered, focused, and in control of my internal state than ever before.

If you feel like you are a slave to your moods or constantly living in your head, please give this book a chance. It is not a quick fix, but a deep dive into how to actually live your life. text:
The package comes with two jar openers. I'm still not sure what to do with the second one because my kitchen isn't all that large, so for now I guess I've got a spare. :) I was a little skeptical of the adhesive, because not only does the jar opener need to stick upside down to the bottom of the cabinet, but it also needs to resist the torque of turning the jar every time you use it. Well, so far so good. It's still adhering to my cabinet bottom and it still works.

There are these little metal teeth on one side of the v-shaped recess. You just slide the jar into the recess as far as it will go and turn. The metal teeth grip the lid, so when you turn, you're actually unscrewing the jar from the lid instead of the lid from the jar. And it's really easy. Admittedly, I don't have arthritis in my hands, so I can't say how easy it would be with arthritis. But I am a single woman with limited arm and grip strength. Jars can be a challenge. Opening them with this is safer than banging on the edge of the lid with the handle of a butter knife. And easier, too.

I'd give it 5 stars, but I can't help but wonder about the longevity of the adhesive. Maybe if it's hanging upside down under my cabinet a year from now I'll come back and give it the 5th star. And yes, I did get this item at a reduce price in order to review it, but that does not effect my review. If you don't have integrity, what have you got?

title: Exceeded My Expectations In Every Way!
text:
Reign of Shadows exceeded my expectations in every way and kept me on my toes the entire story. Danger around every corner, romance, and adventure had me loving every second of Reign of Shadows. I was seriously hooked until the last sentence, and I defiantly did not want it to end there. Luna is an exceptional heroine in this novel, even with her disadvantages she is stronger and tougher than most of the other survivors left in her world. I could not help but want to root for her in every way.

There is a bit of romance, and I love that it does not come out forced as sometimes I find other book will do just to have a romance aspect to the story. It has a natural feeling to it, and it even acts like a beacon of hope in a world of eternal darkness. With switching points-of-view, readers get to experience the story from both Luna’s perspective and Fowler’s perspective. I have always been a fan of the multiple viewpoint stories, as I think it provides a 360 view of the story and the characters. I think it is a needed feature in Reign of Shadows as these two characters both have many thoughts and secrets that only readers get to experience through the changing perspective.

The setting and world building of Reign of Shadows is perfect. It is a dark and creepy world where dark dwellers rise up from the ground every day to eat anything living and without any real sunlight, survivors of the eclipse on get one hour of peace when the dark is just bright enough to drive the dwellers back underground. The description of the dwellers were detailed enough to nearly give me nightmares after reading Reign of Shadows.

This is the first book of Sophie Jordan’s that I have had the chance to read, but I have always heard amazing things about her other books. Now I know that I have definitely been missing out, and I am setting to rectify that mistake as soon as possible. Her writing sucks you deep in the story and holds you there until the very end brings you back to reality. Only the truly best stories can offer that type of hold over a reader.

title: Gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful
text:
Sabaal is a captive Jakkattu imprisoned on Earth by the Mezna priests who experiment on her. Javan 6ix is a tek - half Miscegenate, half machine - beginning to question his life in the city. Norwood Thorne is too smart for a human, too inquisitive for a man, leading his sister Julip down the path of questioning the Temple, the Mezna and all the history they've learnt on the Rez.

Sabaal's escape is the part of the catalyst that throws them all together, leading them to question whether everything the Mezna has been telling them is true. Because beyond their fences, the Feral - the Undone as they name themselves - have information that will turn their understanding of the world upside down.

The Jakkattu Vector is action-packed, with Tyler propelling you from one scene to another, giving you glimpses of the truth, glimmers of the lies these human-Mezna hybrids have grown up with, expecting you to piece them all together before the horrifying reveal. In between, she engages your emotions with the innocence of the young Thornes as they grow up, navigating the thin line between independence and insolence in their quest for truth. And then she feeds you heartbreak on a platter.

The Jakkattu Vector is gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful as each of strand of humanity - human, Miscegenate, Undone - come to terms with who they are and what the Mezna has done to them.

Note: I received an ARC from Novel Publicity in exchange for an honest review as part of a blog tour.

title: An Amish Love
text:
"An Amish Love" is a compilation of 3 novellas centering around 3 different people living in Amish civilizations. Written by Kelly Long, "A Marriage of the Heart" tells the story of Rachel Yoder, an Amish girl who has been raised by her strict father after her mother's death. Tired of her father's and the Amish rules, Yoder quickly marries Joseph Lambert, an Amish man who has only recently returned to the Plain way. Long tells Yoder's story of falling in love with her husband and facing her demons. "What the Heart Sees" by Kathleen Fuller tells the story of Ellie Chupp, a young Amish woman who lost her sight as well as her best friend in a horrible accident. When her best friend's former fiance shows up, Ellie's attempts to deal with her disability are disrupted. However, love is just around the corner for Ellie. "Healing Hearts" by Beth Wiseman tells the story of Naaman and Levina Lapp. After 30 years of marriage, they are facing an empty nest, which is something that Naaman especially cannot deal with. He leaves for year, but when he returns he finds that things are not as he hoped they would be. Levina is cold and confused, dealing with whether or not she can trust the man who left her.

I found these three novellas to be enjoyable. Easy to read and interesting, they offer insight to the lives of the Amish, as well as insight into the lives of people in general. The stories are heartwarming and touching, and I would definitely recommend the book.

title: Live in Gratitude (Not in Greed)
text:
Concerned about "the scary stuff" in the classical Grimm's Fairy Tales, author Susan Meredith chose to rewrite in a softer style. This 2010 soft-cover, 20 page story is nicely populated with colored illustrations on about every other page. This is a story that discourages greed and encourages love and kindness.

In our story, a simple fisherman lives by the sea with his pretty wife. He loves her deeply and works long hours to provide her with nice things to make her happy, but she was never happy. What she had was never enough. One day, he accidentally caught an enchanted flounder. Lady fish "Lorraine" was a beautiful fish with big green eyes and red eyelashes. She spoke, begging for her release, explaining that she was an enchanted princess who was never happy with what she had. She wished for more and more, until she wished too much and "poof". Now she could only grant wishes for others; nothing for herself. Because of his kindness, Lorraine offered the fisherman a wish as he returned her to the sea, but he declined, saying he had everything he needed to make him happy.

Well, you guessed it! When the fisherman returned home and told his wife, she became very angry. SHE wanted more and insisted he return to the sea and ask Lorraine for a larger house. The wife got her wish, but she continued to ask for more and more. Each time the fisherman went to see Lorraine, they chatted like friends and Lorraine granted the wish. Meanwhile, the wife acted as though her husband was no longer good enough for her and her fine house, money, and servants. On his last trip, Lorraine suggested he send his wife instead, if she still wanted more. The wife came, and as you may have guessed, she wished one wish too many and "poof".

Enchanted princess Lorraine changed back to a beautiful woman and rowed ashore to the fisherman.

Without violence or scary stuff, the story illustrates karma nicely - what goes around comes around - you reap what you sow, etc. It also encourages love and gratitude, and discourages being caught up in greed over material things.

Nice value lesson for children, written well, easy to understand, pretty to look at--a winner all around. Even my inner child enjoyed the story!

It is frustrating because the actual performance of the device is decent, but what good is a piece of tech if you cannot even turn it on reliably? I should not have to baby a power button or worry that it will snap off the motherboard if I press it too hard. This is a massive failure in quality control and structural design. Save your money and buy something from a brand that actually invests in durable components. I will be returning this immediately and looking for a replacement that isn't held together by hope and cheap plastic.

text: Even when the plot or the theme doesn't do it for me, Dean Koontz's descriptive skill and unique turn of phrase can usually give me some enjoyment of his books. This time, it wasn't enough. Plenty of description, but  all too dark. Too many characters with too many sub-plots, too much jumping from scene to scene, too many chapters,  too many slimy monsters, too gruesome, too disgusting... It was as if the author had 55 ideas for horror stories, couldn't settle on which one to write, and tried to pack them all into one book. There even seemed to be a veiled attempt at "equal opportunity"--old folks, youngsters, Whites, Oriental, Asian, disabilities... I kept reading, thinking somewhere, somehow there would be a point to all the madness. if one existed, it eluded me completely, and at the end I just wondered why I had bothered. I'll stick with the Odd Thomas books. They at least have some fey humor to lighten the mood.

title: The Birth of a Conservative Movement
text: I have to say that this is one of the few books that I have read that has explained a subject in a way that has radically changed the way I think about a subject. While many critics have pointed to the adoption of the "Southern Strategy" by the Republican Party that has allowed them to gain control of the South, I can think of no other author that has explained it in such a methodical and clear way and with a crucial  distinction.  In fact Kruse argues that what has been characterized as that Souther Strategy is in fact a Suburban Strategy.  The main point of the book is that much of the modern day conservative movement can trace it roots back to the resistance to integration in the late 50's, 60's and 70's  and that Atlanta and its metro area is the perfect example of this shift that occurred nation wide.  What makes this book so good is that it does not assume anything and traces the events in very meticulous detail describing the constantly shifting alliances in the black/white coalition in Atlanta and the though processes on both sides of the issues and while I personally found it very difficult to be sympathetic to those wanting to maintain the status quo,  after reading this book I could see how they got to the ideological point that they re now.  This book is a must read for anyone interested  in the History of political movements in American and the south especially!

title: Better than the movie, but still one of Marvel's weaker '90s efforts.
text:
A decent tale that works better than the Infinity War movie, especially where the character of Thanos is concerned. Even so, this is far from an impressive story arc, and one that becomes muddled and too crammed with characters for its own good. These kind of stories are also difficult to effectively tell when you have a nigh-omnipotent being involved. Marvel still had some great comics in the early '90s like Gruenwald's run on Captain America and Mark Bagley's artistry on Spider-Man, but this book was a sign of things to come as comic plot lines became so mixed up and convoluted that it hurt the industry so badly Marvel nearly went bankrupt.

The best and most effective Marvel superhero crossover is still the original 12-issue Secret Wars series, released in 1984 (and one that had the most lasting consequences, ie Spider-Man's black suit, the Thing leaving the Fantastic Four, etc). Infinity Gauntlet's worth a read, but fails to deliver in its promised scope, and certainly a tale that isn't, by any means, a pivotal moment in Marvel comicdom.

title: Great for costumes, not daily use
text:
I purchased these colored contact lenses for a themed party, and for that specific purpose, they worked out great. The color is vibrant and really pops, which is exactly what I wanted to complete my costume. They looked fantastic in photos and I received several compliments throughout the night on how striking they were.

However, I want to be clear that these are not meant for daily wear. While they looked good, they weren't the most comfortable lenses I have ever worn. After about four or five hours, my eyes started to feel a bit dry and irritated. They have a slightly thicker feel than my prescription lenses, which makes them feel a bit more restrictive on the eye. If you are looking for something to wear for a full work week or long hours every day, I would suggest investing in a higher-end medical brand.

That being said, for a one-time event or a few hours of cosplay, they are a perfect choice. They are affordable and achieve the visual effect perfectly without breaking the bank. I didn't experience any major blurring of vision, just some mild discomfort toward the end of the evening. As long as you manage your expectations and use plenty of rewetting drops, you should be fine. I would definitely buy them again for another costume, but I will stick to my regular contacts for my everyday life.

title: The Irish Banana Review
text:
Ask the Passengers is exactly the type of book you think you're getting when you read the summary: It's a book about a teenage girl who is trying to sort out her life and figure out who she is and who she wants to be. And yes, it has the added twist of the main character coming to terms with her sexual orientation.

I was a little surprised at how ordinary Astrid felt. Not that I expected her to be some dramatic, overblown character, but I felt like there was nothing spectacular that set her apart from a lot of the other teenage girls I read about in contemporary novels. Her parents don't get her--her mom is more concerned with her sister and her dad is fairly oblivious. That just felt formulaic to me. Aside from the lesbian angle to the story, Astrid felt like any other girl dealing with feelings for that special someone, but unsure of how to express them.

This book is all about emotion. I expected that going in, and A.S. King really does a nice job of expressing those emotions. She phrases things splendidly, and I truly enjoy her writing style. The story flowed nicely. It wasn't overly long or excessively wordy, which could have been an easy pitfall to stumble into.

Overall, this book was exactly what I expected, but that's what disappointed me. I was hoping for something that would wow me. Something I could get really excited about and sink into. The setting is a small town where everyone knows everyone's business, but again, that just felt so done already. I feel like I've read variations of this novel before, but the way King wrote it kept me engaged to the end.

text:

Everyone (especially the stalwart Dungeons & Dragons players disappointed with the watered down D&D latest editions) loves the game system and basic premise: to become emperor at all costs (even at the expense of the other players). In that respect, it's like Celebrity Apprentice or Survivor in that the players work together but all are really scheming to outdo each other to eventually rise to such power as to become Emperor or Empress.

The whole game has an open spell system (this book [[ASIN:0692088644 The Adventurer's Rulebook: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]] ) where you create your own spells with a straightforward point system, 10 huge magical fighting arts (this book and the Storyteller's Codex) with 40 fighting art powers each, nonmagical Talents for fighters and thieves, politicians and assassins, and much more.

The system uses d10s only, and the opposed roll system is perfect. It allows the weaker characters a chance against the great characters, as in real life. Overall, it's a great game, in my humble opinion, and a great learning tool for math, vocabulary, and yes, even Latin!

To get a feel for the game, because it is costly (but it is well worth it as these are premium 8.5x11" full color laminate hard cover books), people should order the three available novels:

[[ASIN:1543132170 Mirror Motives: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 1)]]
[[ASIN:1543141161 The Starborn War: Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age (Immortal Empires Sextology) (Volume 2)]]
[[ASIN:0692076018 Keeper of the Myst (Immortal Empires of the Seventh Age) (Volume 3)]]

as well as the other core rulebook for the game:
[[ASIN:0692088660 The Storyteller's Codex: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]]

text:
I bought this sticker and paste book for my preschooler, and it has honestly been one of the best purchases I have made for their early learning journey. It is much more effective than just looking at a flashcard because it turns learning into a game.

Since we started using this book, I have noticed a significant improvement in my child's fine motor skills and their ability to identify both uppercase and lowercase letters. The progression of the activities is well-paced, moving from simple recognition to more complex placements. It feels like a comprehensive tool that bridges the gap between play and education.

I would highly recommend this to any parent or teacher looking for a screen-free way to introduce literacy. It is durable, colorful, and provides genuine value for the price. The product itself seems decent enough once it is actually on the handlebars, but getting it to that point is a nightmare. The installation instructions are incredibly vague and seem to be written for a completely different model. 

If you follow the installation instructions exactly as they are written, be ready for problems. I spent over an hour trying to align the brackets only to realize the provided screws were slightly too short for my setup, forcing me to run to the hardware store for replacements. Even then, the tension nuts didn't lock properly, and I had to keep tightening them every few miles just to keep the mirrors from vibrating or angling downward.

It is frustrating because the glass quality is fine, but the assembly process is a headache. A product in the sports and outdoors category should be rugged and easy to install, but this feels like a project. I wouldn't say the mirrors are broken, but the lack of clear guidance and poor hardware fit makes them hard to recommend. Save yourself the frustration and look for a brand that actually tests their instructions before shipping the product.

title: Waaay better than the Swann I replaced
text:
[[VIDEOID:7ae84ae66b1c39445d7e5289bdae27ae]] I live in a 2nd story apartment and installed a Swann 2.4GHz wireless that I picked up from the local hardware store about a year ago. I installed it after scaring off some would-be car thief's. I decided to replace it because one of my receivers went out and I replaced it with the standard Astak 2.4GHz wireless receiver. I was impressed with the receiver (w/remote) and so I thought I'd give these cameras a try (the Swann was very choppy and I had to mess with the brightness controls in the software I use, a lot). I use the second receiver to hook to the TV in my living room. The cameras and receiver are in the same location as when I was using the Swann.

These cameras are way better than the Swann. The video that comes with this review was taken from my PC (I wire it through a Roxio RCA to USB connector) and use a freeware program to capture it (Debut). There are three walls between my computer and the cameras.

Others post about bad reception because of wireless routers. I don't use one, but there are several that appear in my wireless network list on my Windows PC. To be fair, they could have changed their routers after I installed the Swann a year ago.

Downside: The audio is choppy and has static. I don't use the audio; I didn't use the audio with the Swann, either. This is the reason for my "low" marks. Also, in the manual I discovered that in low light the cameras will switch to black and white. However, as you can see from the video, the b/w hasn't switched on. There is a big flood light in my parking lot which may be the reason. Color 24/7. Judge for yourself.

Tip: you may need to adjust the antenna on the receiver to get the lowest amount of static. I've found that moving it about 20 degrees at a time lets you see the difference.

Well worth the money. I hope this helps.

title: 3.5 Stars
text:
Story: I liked this story much more than the first book of the series (Need). I found that this plot line is better developed and more captivating. I wanted to keep reading and to know what was going to happen. And the end of the novel made me itch to read the third of the series. Unlike the first book (where I pretty much predicted everything that was going to happen), this book was different. It surprised me! Yay! That is an accomplishment in my eyes. One BIG surprise in particular really took me off guard. Ahhh! If you read this book, you will know what I'm talking about!

Characters: All the main characters are the same, likeable characters. Zara develops quite nicely in this book. And there is a new character, Astley, who I think I like. Astley is the new king pixie in town, but he claims to be different - he claims to be good. I like the way he is presented (just hope we can trust him!).

Writing: The writing quality is better in this book. It is still a bit weak, but it was able to captivate my interest. There are a few errors (or typos), but nothing really worth mentioning. I only mention the errors because there were soooo many in the first book. Big improvement here!

Uniqueness/Creativity: This book was also much better in the uniqueness and creativity department. Jones came up with unique and creative elements that I've never heard of before. So, yay! Good for her! And I didn't feel like I was reading Twilight this time!!

Overall: Overall, this book was good. It kept my interest so that I wanted to keep reading. I am itching to read the third book of the series! Can't wait to see what happens! Would I recommend this book? I would recommend it to anyone who really liked Twilight by Stephanie Meyer. If you are bothered by weak quality of writing, then I would suggest staying away. It's a good story, but the quality is a bit weak. Side note: I totally like how the king pixies need a queen in order to be strong(er) - I think it's awesome that women are needed by the men in this way! Hehe :)

title: Didn’t last a day
text:
I really wanted to love this product because the descriptions made it sound like the perfect solution for my dog. I have a medium-sized lab who is energetic but not particularly aggressive with his toys, so I expected this to hold up for at least a few weeks. Unfortunately, it didn’t even last a full day.

I’ve bought much cheaper toys from the grocery store that lasted longer than this.

The quality of the material is very disappointing. It felt sturdy enough when I first took it out of the package, but it clearly cannot withstand any actual play. My biggest concern is the safety risk. I found small bits of the stuffing and plastic pieces on the rug, which is dangerous for a dog that likes to chew and swallow things. I spent a good twenty minutes cleaning up the debris and making sure my pet hadn't eaten any of the fragments.

I am very frustrated because I paid a premium price for what I thought was a durable, high-quality pet supply. Instead, I ended up with a pile of trash and a potential choking hazard in my house. I would not recommend this to anyone with a dog that actually likes to use their toys. Save your money and buy something that is actually built to last.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I decided to upgrade my home office setup and make the switch to this professional-grade desk organizer after using a cheap plastic tray for years. On paper, this product does everything it claims to do. The build quality is certainly an improvement over the budget options, and the aesthetic fits perfectly with my modern office decor. When it first arrived, I was impressed by the weight of the materials and how sturdy it felt on my mahogany desk.

However, the actual user experience has been a bit of a mixed bag. While the overall construction is solid, the attention to detail in the design is lacking. For a product at this price point, I expected the compartments to be more intuitive. I found that while the large slots are great for notebooks, the smaller pen holders are oddly shallow. If you use a standard fountain pen or a longer gel pen, they tend to lean at an angle or slide out entirely if the desk is bumped.

The biggest issue for me is the non-slip grip on the bottom. The product description mentions high-quality rubber feet, but in reality, they are small adhesive pads that started peeling off after only two weeks of use. Now, the metal base occasionally scratches my desk surface when I slide it to reach my keyboard. I have to be incredibly careful moving it, which defeats the purpose of having an efficient workspace.

Assembly was straightforward, though the instructions were printed in a font so small I needed a magnifying glass to read them. It took about ten minutes to put together, but one of the screws didn't thread properly, leaving a slight wobble in the main shelf.

In summary, it is a decent product that looks great from a distance, but it fails on the small, practical details that actually matter during a ten-hour workday. If you are prioritizing looks over absolute functionality, you will probably be happy with this purchase. But if you are looking for a precision-engineered tool to optimize your workflow, you might want to keep looking. It is a step up from the basics, but it doesn't quite reach the level of quality I expected for the cost. It gets the job done, but it isn't perfect.

title: A Colorful Spectrum of Poetry and Painting
text:
Victoria Franks paints pictures with oil and with words, each complementing the other. Her book of poetry and art The Aroma of Coffee is colorful and sensual. From the mountains of South America and the deserts of Arizona to the swamps and shores of Northwest Florida, Franks details the unique beauty she perceives.
Her work covers the gamut of pride in country and despair at war and loneliness to passion, love, and joy. Her poetry shows us the simple yet difficult life of Columbians alongside the complexities of their struggle. Every topic she covers resounds with insightful truth.
Flavored with chocolate, potatoes and corn, mojitos and margaritas, the aroma of coffee is merely a tease. Her work is colored with every hue of the spectrum and accented with Spanish words that roll off the tongue as well as the page, their English definition less important than their fluidity.
Readers easily see the pictures of her words and infer the meanings just below the surface of her paintings. Franks travels effortlessly from one medium to the other and takes the reader with her.

title: Beautiful colorful illustrations
text:
I bought this book primarily as a gift for my niece, but after flipping through the pages, I found myself spending hours admiring it. I have purchased many children's books over the years, but the artwork in this particular volume is on an entirely different level. The colors are incredibly vivid and saturated, making every single page feel like a miniature piece of gallery art.

The quality of the paper is also worth mentioning, as it is thick enough to prevent bleed-through and has a matte finish that makes the colors pop without creating a distracting glare.

It is rare to find a book where the images truly complement the narrative rather than just filling space. These illustrations add layers of emotion and atmosphere that the words alone could not convey. My niece was absolutely captivated by the imagery, and she keeps asking to read it again and again just so she can look at the pictures. 

Even for an adult, there is something deeply soothing and inspiring about the artistic style. It is clear that the illustrator put a tremendous amount of passion into this project. If you are looking for a book that will spark a child's imagination or if you simply appreciate high-quality artistic work, this is a must-have for your collection. It is a stunning addition to our bookshelf and one of the most visually appealing books I have ever owned. I highly recommend it to everyone.

In Bloodhound, Beka is in Port Caynn, searching for the origin of the counterfeited coins that have been popping up in Corus. While the story is enjoyable, the length is not. By page 400, I was wishing that I was at the last page. The end seems to drag on without any resolution. It doesn't help that 'Beka' keeps writing in her diary that she is tired and must stop writing. I would think at her age and maturity, she wouldn't feel the need to write in her diary as if she were talking to it.
The final aspect that was irritating was the very casual, nonchalant way Pounce was disposed of from the list of characters. It was very poorly done, and he was inserted back into the story just as poorly.

As a final thought, would Beka laugh at the irony of knowing that her descendants would have the blood of Trebond as well?

title: Fits my Mosin Nagant 91/30
text:
I was a bit skeptical about ordering this online because finding accessories that actually fit the Mosin Nagant 91/30 can be a real headache. There are so many variations and modifications out there that you often end up with something that is just a fraction of an inch off, making it useless. However, I am happy to report that this fits my rifle perfectly.

The quality of the materials is impressive for the price point. It feels rugged and durable, which is exactly what you want when dealing with a surplus rifle that was built for war. The installation was straightforward and didn't require any modification to the stock or the barrel. It slides right into place and stays secure, even after a full day at the range with repeated recoil.

In terms of performance, it does exactly what it is supposed to do. It adds a level of utility and protection that the original rifle lacked, and it doesn't interfere with the cycling of the bolt or the overall balance of the firearm. It is rare to find a third-party accessory that respects the original dimensions of the 91/30 this well.

If you are looking for something that provides a snug, secure fit without the need for filing or forcing it into place, this is the one to get. It saved me a lot of time and frustration. I highly recommend this to any Mosin owner looking to upgrade their gear without compromising the integrity of the rifle.

title: Limited, superficial, and incomplete (for those who know0
text:
For those who don't know the depth and breadth of Qigong as field of endeavor (not a singular art) with very diverse practices, this is a taste-tester's manual on the topic concerning one of the oldest Qigong systems on record. The problem is ...

(1) it only covers two of the five animals from the ancient sage physician Hua Tou. Which means one's practice is incomplete and out of balance for this particular system.

(2) that no modern scholars are truly certain of how these exercises were conducted, since we have only the sage physician's written descriptions (and not extensive ones) mixed with some cave drawings, and

(3) there are better works that attempt to address not only their own speculations on how these exercises were conducted but also attempt to support such with scholarship and reasoning, drawing on comparative arts inside and outside of the Qigong field, and stepping well beyond mere two sentence sketchy definitions of romanized Chinese terms... as is the case in this book.

If you would like a simple and short manual with direct instructions for soft exercises that might not do enough for you, then maybe this is for you. Or if you're another new ager looking for your next step on a path likely leading nowhere, then this is for you. If you want to explore the range of speculations on this ancient Qigong system, then you might also consider buying it... but only after you've acquired other more comprehensive works on the topic.

You may find yourself ignoring the crossword and reading, say, the movie or book review from 1990. Or just perusing the ads.

The editors have taken one puzzle from each year back to 1942 and printed its entire page.

The downside to the book so far (I started at 2016 and worked backwards) is when you get to the Eugene Maleska years (77-93) (Oh, let me
correct myself: it's Eugene T. Maleska, not to be confused with all those other Eugene Maleska's in the USA). That "T" might tell you all you
need to know about his puzzles. They reek of what passed for knowledge way back when: obscure Broadway shows, "great" writers that most
people have never heard of, French language (by the way, there was an error in one of those), capitols of regions of small nations etc.

I have another compilation of NY Times puzzles that goes back decades which is very challenging because what passed for common knowledge back then is obscure now. However, that's not my issue with Maleska.

Altogether, this is a great gift for any crossword puzzler; mine was a gift as well.

text: When a book is released around the time of an author's death the literary world seems to shower him/her with an insane amount of praise that one has to wonder if death didn't come calling would would this book be so highly praised.  This is a short book (only about 244 pages which is slightly misleading because of page margins and text size this book is much shorter).  It's plot is compelling and it is wonderfully descriptive.  I found  Matthiessen' s tendency to switch between writing from the point of view of the main character to casual observer confusing and wish he would have stuck to one or the other.  The main character's purpose for being in this place and time (when you finally learn why)  is a great and equally tragic story line and by itself is enough to carry the reader.  The introduction of all minor characters just dilutes the story and introduces a bunch of characters that we don't care about and have absolutely no reason to care about.  Overall I gave this book 3 stars simply because the cast of characters and their relationship to the story is unmoving and distracting from the good aspects of this book.  It would be silly to tell someone not to read this book because the reality is, this is such a short book that even if you hated it you're not investing a huge chunk of your time.  It's not like reading a 1,000 page epic like PILLARS OF THE EARTH where if you hate it or get bored you've still got hundreds of pages to get through before you can properly decide what you're overall opinion is.

title: A Very Good Electric Shaver for Sensitive Skin
text:
As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

title: Alamo Questions
text:
Chariton explores a number of questions revolving around the tragedy of Alamo. Most of the questions he explores are, in fact, not legends but legitimate questions as to what did or did not happen in an around the time that the Alamo was attacked and the defenders slaughtered. Generally I agree with Chariton's deductions although I also believe that all testimony regarding the Zuber must regarded with extreme suspicion. Zuber claimed that he got his information from Louis Rose, the supposed only deserter from Alamo. In a manner resembling Thucidides, Zuber admitted embellishing [making up] Travis' final speech to the troops, including the famous 'line in the sand'. In my opinion, if Zuber lied about anything, then it should be rightfully assumed that he lied about everything.

I think Zuber's testimony is an insult to all the men who died at Alamo. Their heroism stands by itself and required no second hand editorialism. I'll go even further than that to proclaim my own belief that Louis Rose--if he ever existed--never testified to Zuber. Zuber made up the entire story 'whole-cloth'.

Ron

title: Great for documents.  Horrible for photos. Get it on sale and it's a steal!
text:
If I could do it, it would be 3.5 stars. Here is the skinny:

Pros:

Scanning and printing of normal documents is great.

You can scan to a network folder, your computer, to FTP, to a USB stick, or email as an attachment right from the printer. It's more than reasonable for first page out and multiple pages.

Easy setup. Printing from your phone is easy. Internet printing capability (print from anywhere, ready when you get home).

Toner is like all color laser printers, relatively expensive for the brand name but much cheaper than inkjet in the end.

Have been successful faxing using a OBI200 and a Google Voice number so very handy when you need to occasionally fax but don't have a physical land-line in the house.

While it isn't silent, it is not unreasonably loud. My old Canon inject makes more racket (clicks, clacks, bangs) when it starts up.

I have never had wake from stand-by issues. Wakes from sleep pretty fast.

Cons:

It is big (small con). But all color lasers tend to be in this size and up as they need to be able to hold and align all those cartridges. As a matter of fact, due to the pull-out tray design and smaller physical cartridges this is probably on the smaller side of color laser printers.

Flatbed color scanning from your computer of things like photographs, is IMHO HORRIBLE, with out of whack colors and edge diffractions and all sorts of oddities. It's to the point that I wonder if it's defective. Oddly, scanning of documents seems pretty good. I need to do some experimentation to see if it's a software driver issue or something but I've scanned direct into Photoshop, Picassa, and Acrobat and they all are pretty sub-par. The computer driver scanning controls are now very basic, not like they used to be years ago with much more control...maybe that's part of the problem.

Also, when _printing_ photographic type images the colors are massively over-saturated...okay for presentation graphs, charts, and stuff but again waaaayy off base for anything else. While I understand this is a business oriented machine, even businesses scan/print photographs and it shouldn't be this far off (a lack of functionality/settings in the printer driver could be partly to blame).

Issue #1: Stud-in-residence (the police chief) calls ex-stud (contractor/carpenter) "Bob the Builder" - more than once. Both are (understandably) concerned for the MC's safety. When they are trying to talk her into staying safe, they say things like "don't be such a Nancy Drew" or "you're running off like Dora the Explorer".

Seriously? Two adult macho males referring to children's TV programming? I would have let Bob the Builder pass (though it twanged something in my head), but Nancy Drew and Dora the Explorer?

Issue #2: In a small section the author's editor apparently went on break. In the space of just a few pages, I read "peaked into the refrigerator", "share's my blood" and "for Cinnamon and I". All three of these are glaring errors that shouldn't have existed had the writer paid attention through middle school English/Grammar classes.

Having griped about those two issues, I must reiterate that I really liked the book. It had a slight comic book feel to it - A good slice of humor, quirky supporting characters, some adventure and danger, and an ending that I didn't figure out until it was time to do so.

title: Amstaff mom approved!!!!
text:
This collar is a life saver!
We have a nearly one year old American Amstaff that is the single most stubborn hard headed dog in the entire world. After paying ungodly amounts of money on training & behavior classes, we were at wits end with our boy. Any time we let him out the door he would take off like his tail was on fire & it was nearly impossible to get him to come back until he was good and ready. This collar has made a gigantic improvement in his behavior outside. We don't even normally have to use the shock function. Most of the time the vibrate option scares him into action & works perfectly.

The packaging was great, while there were little to no instructions in the product box, or on the box, with a little trial & error we figured it out pretty quickly.
The charger seems to work amazing. As instructed I charged the unit for 6 hours after opening. We've been using the collar for about a 1-2 weeks now and it's STILL RUNNING on THAT FIRST CHARGE! Granted we only use the collar for potty & outside time. So that's probably a big factor in our extended battery life.

We haven't had any issues with the collar itself. My pupper is a very broad Amstaff so his neck girth is pretty substantial, and the collar included fit with plenty of room to spare. We also have not had any skin issues with where the prongs sit on our boy. Again, he doesn't continuously wear the collar, which is probably a contributing factor. I could see where the prongs could potentially be an issue if the use of the unit wasn't closely supervised. Leaving it on your dog for long periods of time, in the same spot, without adjusting could definitely be hazardous to a dog.

All in all, we absolute live this collar. It was extremely affordable and a great quality for the price. Honestly, I'm surprised it's not higher. Great purchase.

title: More like "Helping Badger Overcome Depression"
text: I was surprised to see this book so breezily reviewed.  I myself found it disturbing.  There are lots of good books around that deal with bad moods--"Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Really Bad  Day" and "Today I Feel Silly & Other Moods That Make My  Day" come to mind.  This book goes way beyond moodiness and knocks on  the door of clinical depression.  First, the animals find Badger sitting in  his chair in the dark.  When they switch on the light, Badger snaps at them  to turn it off and leave him be.  The other animals leave, but Mole is  worried about Badger so he stays and cleans up the place a bit. Badger  eventually speaks: "I'm sorry about this. 'Spect I'll get over it.  But right now, I'm just no good, you know.  No good for anything."  Mole tells him they'll "just wait".  Eventually the animals call  a doctor.  Badger refuses to see her and sends Mole out to get rid of her  and the other animals trying to help:  "Close the curtains," he  begged Mole.  "Keep them away."  Then we have a scene where Mole  watches Badger "staring and dozing and turning heavily in his  chair."  YIKES! And then, just when you're sure Mole is going to be  calling the suicide hotline, things turn rosy and child-appropriate again.  Mole comes up with the idea of an Awards Ceremony (this causes Badger's  eyes to move "sharply for the first time in days").  Badger and  all the other animals attend.  Badger wins all sorts of awards for being a  good person/badger.  At last he feels "appreciated" and is happy.  Everyone dances.  I was confused (and creeped out).  My child was  confused:  "How come he wants to sit in the dark?...How come he  doesn't want the doctor to help him?...Doesn't he like the other animals  anymore?...Does he like them better now that they had a party for  him?"  If this had been a book to help children understand  depression--a book with an appropriate resolution and ending--it would have  been fine.  If this had been a book about a badger who was feeling glum and  unappreciated, who was then cheered up by an awards ceremony, it would have  been fine.  But this book is a bizarre marriage of the two and it is AWFUL.

text:
I was a Wacom user for about 12 years, using a Intuos v3 large- Now don't get me wrong, it's not that this tablet is necessarily bad, but I just don't think it's for me. While the drawing surface is about the same size as the intuos 3 I had, the size overall is quite a bit smaller, and I need larger tablets because of my carpal tunnel. I tend to draw with my whole arm/elbow, so it's difficult to adjust to after having a bigger tablet for such a long time.

The surface is also incredibly matte which is... odd feeling? The buttons both on the tablet and the pen are fairly inconveniently placed even for a right handed user I tend to press them often when moving to type or holding the edge as I draw. I can't imagine how bad it'd be for a left handed user. Now to the button on the pen; something about the placement is just... off. I never had this issue with my intuos pen, but I CONSTANTLY press it, which turns the pen off. Constantly. I'll be working and turn off my pen about 4-6 times within about 2 hours maybe?

All in all this tablet just isn't for me and was honestly a quick fix for my previous tablet finally dying on me. I am quite confident at the moment that I'll be going back to wacom once I have the extra income to do so.

Pros:

• The desktop shortcut to the tablet menu is actually quite helpful. It makes it easy to adjust the overall pen pressure of the tablet.
• 8 extra pen nibs in the bottom of the pen stand.

Cons:

• Incredibly matte drawing surface. Which in my personal opinion not as nice as a nice glossy, smooth, drawing surface.
• Shortcut buttons are super inconvenient and poorly placed.
• Button on pen is very poorly placed. Probably one of my biggest issues so far.

By genetics, I am part English, and completely Western European, and I read this book to better understand my people's history pre-America. I enjoyed Howarth's take on village life of the commoners/peasantry int he first chapter; he details their low stress, and deep sense of belonging and racial/English community. Written 40 years ago, in a story with no non-Whites, it was still acceptable to talk about racial/tribal community as a natural and healthy thing. title: Noise Reduction Techniques
text:
There is a specific topic in this book that I have not seem covered in any of the 25+ book that I have on electromagnetic phenomena. The topic is the shield cut-off frequency of a coaxial cable. Common-mode currents at low frequencies (below a few hundred hertz) cause noise problems with coaxial cables, but signals above tens of kilohertz do not. This is vital data which is apparently not explained in many text books. For me, this topic justifies the cost of the text. Having said that, I am annoyed because the book is quite expensive relative to other books of its size and age. The point is that you have to buy it, but it is expensive to do so.
Even an advanced designer will benefit from this book, although you, like me, won't necessarily want to read all of it. It is sufficient to pick and choose areas of particular interest. The less advanced designer would clearly benefit more and the book would therefore represent better value for them. Given a choice between this one and Morrison's Grounding and Shielding Techniques in Instrumentation, pick this one. This one is more technically accurate and useful.

text: This is kinda a weird item.  Neat idea, but weird.  I have extended magazines that came with my Sig pistol and they fit okay.  The problem with extended mags is they don't fit in most mag holders because they are overly tall and the flap doesn't velcro shut like it should.  The flaps on this pouch grab the velcro with my mags inside, but just barely.  You can fold the flaps back entirely and use the "griptite" feature to hold the magazines.  I keep going back and forth on whether I like the "griptite" design.  It consists of plastic clips that grab the magazines, which fold into the cordura material in a pocket.  Hard to explain, but when you put your mag in the plastic acts as a spring and squeezes your magazine.  The mag slides out with a mild tug.  They make the overall pouch much thicker, probably twice as thick as the magazine would be otherwise.  I think I would prefer a simple pouch over a gee-whiz clippy thing.  I suspect these would be great if you knew you would be standing up while using them (such as on the range or at a match).  If you were crawling around in the dirt with these they still might fall out (even with the "griptite" feature) and your magazines would certainly get dirty.  These are not great for keeping your mags out of the elements.  But i suppose it's a trade off.  They are quite speedy to get out and would make for quick mag changes.  They're cheap enough- try them out for yourself!

title: Lois good on the counter
text:
I bought this counter organizer after spending way too much time digging through cluttered drawers for my daily essentials. I was looking for something that felt sturdy but didn't take up my entire workspace, and this fits the bill quite well. The build quality is solid, and it feels like it will hold up over time even with heavy use in a busy kitchen.

The design is clean and minimalist, which helps make my countertops look a lot more organized and intentional. It holds everything I need in one spot, meaning I no longer have small items sliding around or getting lost under the mail. The dimensions are just right for most standard counters, and it doesn't slide around too much once you have a few things placed on it.

The only reason I am giving it four stars instead of five is that the finish is a bit more matte than it appeared in the product photos. While it still looks great, I was expecting a slightly more polished shine. Additionally, the assembly took a couple of minutes longer than I anticipated because the instructions were a bit vague, but it was nothing a little patience couldn't fix.

Overall, this has been a great addition to my home. It has significantly reduced the visual clutter in my kitchen and has made my morning routine much smoother. If you are looking for a functional, decent-looking way to clear up your counter space, this is a reliable choice. It does exactly what it is supposed to do without being overly complicated. I would recommend it to anyone who needs a bit more structure in their kitchen organization.

title: Great German Built Rower, good quality, heartrate monitor, smooth track, noiseless!
text:
Got this rower as part of my 2014 new years resolution.

AMAZON did a great job delivering on the date they said they would, through their shipper CEVA (for large items).

Put the rower together in 30 mins, minor assembly, and have been using actively daily.

* Very, very quiet...Can watch TV or listen to music easily without distraction

Cons:

I plan to use for years, so quality was important. Kettler is a huge global athletic/gym equipment company (their ping pong tables are what I knew them for).

If you are looking for a top quality rower, that is fluid, silent, and store-able, I highly recommend.

title: A Concise & Well-Written Treatise on Freedom.
text:
This thin book is packed with common sense about politics and freedom. And although I knew most of the positions Ron Paul supports and the evidence for them, I still learned some new things.

My favorite quote from the entire book: "Truth is treason in the empire of lies." Oh man, that's a zinger. And it describes our current political environment perfectly.

My only criticism of the book is minor: He brings up the issue of 9/11 briefly, but speaks as if terrorists were solely responsible for it. I suppose the book would've gotten way off track if he had mentioned it, but there's plenty of evidence that 9/11 was an inside job. And I'm not only referring to "Loose Change." (Take Robin Hordon's testimony, for instance, among many others.)

If we don't make changes, we're bound for tough times ahead. This quote from the book sums up well where we're headed:

"Any government that inflates the money supply runs the risk of hyperinflation, which occurs when the money supply is increased so much as to render the currency completely worthless. [...] The textbook case in the twentieth century took place in Germany in 1923. [...] The result was the complete ruin of the German mark, which German children began gluing together to make kites and German adults burned in order to keep warm." (p. 150-151)
