title: A pleasant read, but could have been much better - 3.5 stars
text:
Meet the Essex sisters: four Scottish ladies recently orphaned and left impoverished with no prospective husbands. Now wards of the perpetually inebriated Duke of Holbrook, their first mission is to marry off their eldest, the witty and sensible Teresa, or Tess, as she prefers to be called.

Growing up without the proper training that other ladies of their kind receive, Tess knows that she must marry in order to support her sisters. But what she didn't expect is that she will immediately catch the eyes of two very eligible English gentlemen. There is the Earl of Mayne, who seems to genuinely like her and whom she will most likely develop a nice, though not passionate, affection for; and then there is the very rich, though just a mere Mister, Lucius Felton, who unnerves her and whose very nearness makes her heart somersault. While Tess knows that either man is a good choice, she is torn when both men ask for her hand in marriage.

While the story started off with a great promise, the focus on establishing the characters of the four sisters overshadows what could have been a really delightful romance between Tess and Lucius. Just when you think we'd finally get some action going between the main characters, the heroine would be involved in her sisters' dramas and so the focus is once again taken away from the romance. However, the interactions between Tess and Lucius when we finally get to the part are rather sweet, and at times, funny. The little banter we get to see between them surely adds to the delight of the story.

Overall, MUCH ADO ABOUT YOU is a pleasant read and holds promise for the stories of the other Essex sisters. Next are KISS ME, ANNABEL (Annabel's story) and THE TAMING OF THE DUKE (featuring Imogen).

title: Not Enthusiastic
text:
OK, first the things I liked about the Littlest Pet Shop. All the parts were easy to assemble with clear instructions. The front panel is hinged so that little hands could get into the shop. Three "littlest pets" were included with the set. (It irks me when these "branded" sets are sold without the action figures.)

Now, for the things I didn't like. Though the sides, front, and base are made of sturdy plastic, the back panel was very thin cardboard. I had four little girls ages 5 to 10 "helping" me assemble the set, although they did more playing than assembling. Before we had gotten all the Deco bits taken off the plastic frames, the back panel had popped out of the frame. To restore it properly, several pieces had to be taken apart. For a play set that retails for $40, seems to me that the back panel could have been made from plastic, too. The sales counter was also a problem. It came in two pieces: the top and the base. The only way I could get the counter top to stay fastened to the base was to attach it with double-sided tape.

The set contains 135 pieces. A few pieces are decals. There are maybe 20 larger pieces. However, the rest are very small plastic pieces, the kind that small pets and toddlers choke on. The kind that children leave all over the floor and you step on in the middle of the night on your way to the bathroom or refrigerator. The kind you're still digging out from beneath the car seat when the child graduates from high school. Enough said?

In spite of my lack of enthusiasm for the Littlest Pets Shop Style Set, the 4 girls loved it. They happily played with everything. They set up the shop, decorated the side walls, the dog house, and the pets with the Deco Bits. They let the monkey swing from the chandelier and gave the pets new names. They just had fun. On their way out the door, the two older girls were asking their mom if they could go to the store. No one had to asked why...

title: Love it!
text:
I did a ton of research before buying this keyboard, i was in the market for a gaming mech keyboard (i even picked this one over the stealth, price diff aside).

This keyboard is beyond amazing, each button depress is smooth and easy- typing on dome keyboards now exhaust my fingers. My niece sat at my computer to show me a site she likes, it literally took her two seconds of typing on it to exclaim "OMG, this keyboard is the keyboard of my dreams". I can't articulate how good this keyboard feels, when my friend's ask, I reply "It's like sex for the fingers".

I also like the 5 macro keys down the left side, they are within easy striking distance and add more keybinds (which insane that i need more, i do have a Naga mouse lol). The back lighting is great as I prefer to play in the dark, and the lockout of the windows button is also a great feature (long nails clipping it during PVP is BAD). The included editing software is easy to use.

As for the sound, is it loud? Yea a bit, obviously it's louder than a normal keyboard, but I actually enjoy it, and joyfully clack the keys. It's really not that loud, maybe if you were in a empty room with high ceilings were it could echo would you find this a issue. I dont really see any gamer that is enough into gaming that they would A. want a mech keyboard, and B. pay this much for a keyboard having an issue with it. Just don't try using it in the same room your GF is sleeping...

Improvements/cons? Wish you could adjust the back light levels and color, and maybe 5 more macro buttons by the space bar would be lovely (i'm sick i know). The ONE con i do have, its that sometimes my space bar sticks, its VERY VERY rare- and i can't say that is actually a design flaw- it could be a cookie cumb or something... heh. So, i wouldnt suggest nibbling on something around it.
Great job Razer. Oh and btw, when i've had issues with past items (naga mouse addon being buggy), the razer tech guys were amazing and intense about figuring out my problem (Screen shots etc).

I joined in the study as much as I was able, since it was the start of a new school year, but watching them at work connecting and learning with those in the community cemented the learning for me.

The Connected Educator: Learning and Leading in a Digital Age is a great book for wherever you are in digital age learning. Chapter 5 is a mini encyclopedia the basic web tools you should use and why to use them. In addition, I believe it is imperative for present and future principals to read Chapter 8, "Transforming Leadership for a Connected World."

Overall, I understood more deeply the philosophy of learning and leadership behind much of what I was learning to do. Now I am more committed than ever to learning and leading in the digital age.

Thanks, Sheryl and Lani.

title: It's not about food
text:
Differently from the movie, this is not a tale about sophisticated food. It deals with the severe restrictions that puritanism imposes on pleasure - and how a tastefull dinner, with the help of some good wines, helps this fundamentalist lutheran aging community to retrieve joy and forgiveness.

In the movie, although the puritan restrictions are present, stress is on the food - the ingredients, the way it is being prepared, the discovery of it by the coachman and Bebette's assitant, and principally the precise description by the general. The transformation of the puritans, from mere tolerance of an extravagance to real appreciation and joy only underines the quality of what is being served.

In the novel, food plays a secondary role, contrasting with the grey sad environment and the equally gray and sad inhabitants of a norwegian community lost in the high north, squeezed between the mountains and an unfriendly see. Stress is on the way a severe pastor has molded the spirit of his daughters and of his few followers, banning all earthly pleasures.

I've decided to read the novel after having a dinner that reproduced the menu of Babette's feast, preceded by the film and a technical explanation by the danish chef. Dinner was excelent and our community did not resemble at all to the inhabitants of the small village - which in the film was moved from Norway to Denmark. I was first surprised by the differences in approach but then I realized that this short novel gives you food for thoughts. While the movie is pure pleasure, the novel is profound.

I recommend it and, if I may suggest, have it complete: the movie, the dinner and the short novel.

title: Sucks for kids. Perfect for adults.
text:
This is an excellent choice if you are trying to drink 8 glasses of water a day. You can take 8 glasses, pour it in all at once, pour the 8 glasses into your container or hydration pack of choice and off you go. Simplicity itself. The pitcher holds at least 16 glasses, so someone else in the family can get their 8 glasses too. I was well hydrated when using this pitcher. CONS: Children 3 - 8 can not handle this pitcher at all. When they try to use the spigot, they tip the whole pitcher accidentally on the floor and it shatters. I did try the metal version of this pitcher, but still fell and still shattered at the plastic. It doesn't have that always pour lid, so they pour it when it is still filtering and water pours every where. I also tried pouring the filtered water in a metal pitcher for them (preferring to avoid plastic) but since it was metal, it was hard to monitor when they'd need a refill so that didn't work great. Finally, they did well with the Zero Water 8 glass round pitcher. Never dropped it once. But you can only put about 3 glasses of water at a time and it is like a 30 minute project to get your 8 glasses filtered. My water consumption honestly went down using that product. But it was the only sensible option. I know they have a glass 40 cup stand. But I just have nightmares of glass and gallons of water on the floor and couldn't bring myself to buy it.

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this wheel to replace a worn-out one on my son's stunt scooter, and overall, I am quite happy with the purchase. When you are looking for a larger wheel, the main goal is usually to get a smoother ride over rougher pavement and a bit more stability at higher speeds. This product definitely delivers on that front.

The build quality is impressive. The core feels sturdy and doesn't seem like it will crack under pressure during jumps or hard landings. The polyurethane material is dense and has a good grip on the road, which gives a lot more confidence when carving or turning sharply. Compared to the smaller stock wheels that came with the scooter, these make a noticeable difference in how the ride feels. The vibration from the asphalt is significantly reduced, and it takes a bit more effort to maintain speed, but it glides much further once you get going.

The installation process was straightforward, although I did have to double-check my bearings. The wheel fits perfectly on the axle without any wobbling. I noticed that the color is slightly different from the images online, but it is still a nice, vibrant shade that looks great on the deck.

The reason I am giving this four stars instead of five is that I noticed a tiny bit of flat-spotting after about two weeks of heavy use. My son tends to skid and brake hard, and while the wheels are durable, they aren't completely immune to wear and tear. I think they are great for general riding and moderate stunts, but if you are a professional-level rider doing extreme grinds every single day, you might find them wearing down faster than the premium high-end brands. However, for the price point, the value is exceptional.

If you are looking to upgrade a basic scooter to make it feel more "premium" and smooth, this is a fantastic choice. It transforms the ride from a bumpy, jittery experience into something much more fluid. I would definitely recommend these to any parent or rider who wants a larger wheel without spending a fortune. Just be mindful of how hard you brake if you want them to last as long as possible. It is a solid, reliable piece of equipment that does exactly what it claims to do.

title: Look What I See
text:
This series entitled, "Look What I See! Where Can I Be?" which includes the previous titles that explored "the neighborhood", "the home", "my animal friends" and "visiting China", now examines "the synagogue" with mixed results. The publisher promotes the book as "exploring a week in Jewish family life", but that week constitutes a rather confused timeline for most adults familiar with Jewish rituals and traditions. The concept is one that is completely appropriate for very young children. An inquisitive toddler and her doll view items relating to Jewish rituals and then, with a turn of the page, we see her and her family photographed at the larger event. For instance, the text reads, "On Sunday, I fell asleep in my stroller. When I woke up, I saw a Kiddish cup." First we view the Kiddish cup in a clear photo, and then the toddler asks, "Where was I? By the Chuppah at a wedding." Within the wedding photo, clever toddlers will notice an apple and also the doll in his stroller. These photos and questions and answers are repeated 7 times for the days of the week and make for an appealing, structured format. However, this format does not work as well in a synagogue as it probably does for "exploring the neighborhood". Confusion abounds as we are led to believe that Rosh Hashana and Simchat Torah fall within the same week, or that apples are an integral part of every Jewish ritual. Confusion continues as the reader assumes the text to be the words of the toddler ("I fell asleep in my stroller"), but the photo then matches what the plastic doll is doing rather than the young girl. Also, the plastic doll, with a droopy, oversized blue kippah, is generally unappealing. Another issue involves the choice of photographs of both people and ritual objects. For example, the lulav is cut off, the dancers are blurry, and the "menorah" they chose to display is the stylized, artistic synagogue wall version, which is certainly not something a toddler would recognize from the home version. This book may work for some families comfortable with Reform traditions, but, in general, it needs to be revamped to appeal to its intended audience of Jewish families with small children.

Reviewed by Lisa Silverman

title: Best of the pre-PEP or pre-W series works
text:
Perhaps because of a lack of publication or perhaps because of a general lack of distribution of his ideas (Peirce tended to write only for other philosophers and logicians), Peirce's philosophical thinking was not well known until Eisele's "New Elements of Mathematics" (NEM), and the Peirce Edition Project's W series: "The Chronological Writings of Charles Sanders Peirce". Buchler's work is easily the best introduction to the work of Peirce prior to the availability of NEM and the W series.

Buchler worked from an earlier collection of Peirce's writings, called the CP series, consisting of 8 volumes of poorly edited papers presented in such a way as to not show the depth, or originality of his thought, or the evolutionary growth in the depth and power of his thought.

Nevertheless, Buchler's volume is still an excellent, easy to read, and easy to understand (relative to Peirce's depth of thinking) introduction to the immensity of the thought of Charles Peirce. I recommend it as a great reading value.

The scale was relatively cheap so I was concerned about its precision and accuracy, so I weight 6 coins to see if the claims could be verified. The test showed the Standard Deviation of the measurements was less that one milligram per gram. As to the accuracy the standard provided was not much use as it was probably used to do the initial calibration of the scale, but it was useful in assessing the repeatability, which was very good. I got 100 grams each time I weighted it. To get an idea about the accuracy I used the coins, which when new have very consistent weights. The coin test showed about 0.25% deviation from what clean new coins should have weighed. As the coins were neither new or clean, in my opinion, this is very good for a scale of this price. As I am going to use the scale to titrate my medicines, the accuracy and repeatability are very important to me. These scales appear to be way within my criteria. The scale appears to be well made, but at this time I have no idea how reliable it is.

Now the bad news: parts of the protective shielding were not included in the package. The vendor promised to send me the missing parts but they have not arrived yet. I’ll update this review in two weeks or so with an assessment of the vendors performance. Update: they arrived!

I have found the scale is repeatable, but is does not respond to a small load change. Say 4 mg plus or minus. The work around is to put pressure on the scale for a second or so and it will adjust the reading correctly. This second delay is a little irritating but it probably deals with air currents and vibrations constantly changing the readings and the microprocessor spending time averaging the readings. I have been titrating one of my meds to 1.375 mg dose, which works out to 60 mg of the ground up tablets and I was able keep 37 doses all with in +/- 1.5%

I have gone through several different nutcrackers over the years, from the cheap handheld ones to the heavy-duty screw types, but this is by far the best one I have ever owned. I bought this for the holiday season to handle a large batch of walnuts and pecans, and it has performed flawlessly. The build quality is impressive; it feels sturdy and well-constructed, not like the flimsy metal tools you often find at big-box stores.

What I appreciate most is the leverage. It requires very little effort to crack even the toughest shells, and it does so without crushing the actual nut inside. I used to struggle with walnuts that were stubborn, but this tool handles them with ease. The grip is comfortable and doesn't slip in my hand, which makes processing a whole bowl of nuts much faster and less frustrating. It is easy to clean and stores away neatly in my kitchen drawer. If you are looking for a reliable, high-quality nutcracker that actually does what it claims to do, look no further. This is a fantastic addition to my kitchen and is well worth the investment for anyone who enjoys fresh nuts.

title: Child of Thorn and Hunger
text:
Note: I have read the story on RoyalRoad, which goes beyond the currently published books. This review stands as a synopsis of what I have read so far.

Fantastic story heavily inspired by Vampire: The Masquerade, showcasing the unnatural dominion of vampires over humans and most other magical creatures. This includes the existence of distinct vampire clans with unique supernatural traits and an inveterate hierarchical vampire society to maintain power and secrecy.

As the main character, Ariane is painfully reborn into a warrior bloodline with an antediluvian psychopath for a progenitor. Abandoned and left to fend for herself, she must navigate the perils of vampire society as an outcast and the lawless American frontier as a woman. As much potential as she has as a vampire, her beginnings leave her weak and at the mercy of far more powerful forces. It is with intelligence and true grit that she must learn to survive and thrive.

But the real struggle for Ariane is to maintain her sense of honor and humanity as she fights against the demands of her nature and the madness of her bloodline. While far from a warrior of light, she is fearless when she chooses to fight for what she believes in and builds bonds of deep friendship with interesting and diverse people. Her acts of kindness are rare, but they shine as genuine and without the avarice and cruelty inherent to her kind.

While she definitely stumbles at times, Ariane remains steadfast to her friends and an anti-hero to those she saves along the way. I hope that her journey keeps her from succumbing to wickedness and allows her to emerge as something special. A dark star in a world of darkness.

I use these bottles to a variety of tasks around the house. One is filled with bleach for aggressive cleaning, such as the bathroom or to kill mold growing outside my house. One is filled with a home-made cleaning mixture of equal parts rubbing alcohol, vinegar, and distilled water (works great on glass!). And the last one is diluted hydrogen peroxide used to treat indoor and outdoor plants. Hydrogen peroxide will break down quickly when exposed to light, so make sure you store it in a dark/cool/dry place.

title: Feels even better than it looks (and no problems in Linux)
text:
When another HTPC-style keyboard finally irritated me enough to replace it, I decided to try the diNovo Edge. In photos, the Edge looks attractive enough, but I always thought that the slimness made it look a little, well, flimsy. After actually getting it and trying it in person, (a) it looks even classier than the photos, and (b) it's got a nice heft and rigidity to it that gives it a feeling of quality I was not expecting. It really is a brushed aluminum piece there, not shiny plastic. Admittedly, it's expensive, but after trying it out I don't think it's disproportionately so.

About the trackpad ("TouchDisc"): I noticed some reviews commenting that it's nothing special. That's partially true; for the most part, it works just like normal laptop trackpad, which is good. The scrolling support has an interesting feature, though: on normal rectangular laptop trackpads, you place your finger at the right edge of the trackpad, and move it up and down to scroll. But you soon hit the top or bottom edge of the trackpad and have to stop. On the diNovo Edge you start the same way, by placing your finger at the right edge, but because it's round you instead move clockwise or counterclockwise to scroll, so you never have to stop. So once you start it scrolling you can just keep spinning your finger in circles around the outside edge over and over, pause, or change direction. The speed and accuracy of this approach are both big improvements, particularly when scrolling up and down long pages.

As for Linux support: no need for special drivers for the support of the main keys or the touchpad. In fact, many of the special media keys worked as expected out of the box, including the volume slider. Depending on what you're using to map keyboard shortcuts, though, not all of the media keys were available to be mapped without some tweaking. For these, a program called "keytouch" (probably available in most package managers) let me program the rest; it included settings for a different diNovo keyboard that seems to work fine for the Edge and includes most of those other keys already.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
I honestly didn't have high expectations when I ordered this, especially given the price point compared to some of the big-name brands I have used in the past. I have been burned by budget home goods before, so I went into this purchase with a bit of skepticism. However, after using it daily for the last three weeks, I can honestly say I am pleasantly surprised.

From a build quality standpoint, it feels sturdy. It doesn't have that cheap, flimsy plastic feel that you often find with generic kitchen gadgets. The design is intuitive, and it fits perfectly into my current setup without taking up too much counter space. The first time I turned it on, I was impressed by how quiet it was. My previous model sounded like a jet engine taking off in my kitchen, but this one is surprisingly discreet, which is a huge plus for those of us who try to get things done while the rest of the house is still asleep.

In terms of performance, it does exactly what it is supposed to do. It is efficient, consistent, and has made my morning routine significantly faster. I haven't noticed any major glitches or malfunctions, and the cleanup process is straightforward, which is usually where these products fail for me.

The only reason I am giving it four stars instead of five is the instruction manual. It was a bit vague and poorly translated in a few sections, which made the initial setup take a little longer than it should have. I had to do a bit of trial and error to figure out the best settings for my specific needs. Additionally, the power cord is slightly shorter than I would prefer, meaning I had to move my appliance closer to the outlet than I wanted.

That being said, those are minor gripes in the grand scheme of things. For the price, the value is exceptional. It performs at a level that rivals products costing twice as much. If you are looking for something that gets the job done without breaking the bank, this is a great choice. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who wants a reliable upgrade for their kitchen without spending a fortune.

If you consider yourself pro-Palestinian, I challenge you to read this text. If you are pro-Israeli, Christian Zionist, or Jewish Zionist, I challenge you to read this text. title: A Literary Spuge
text:
How many creative ways can one pose the vulgar? And we don't mean pose in the effete way, either. Perhaps this book will make you feel like Charles Manson playing the kazoo before an audience of irritable emperor penguins. Maybe.

It is hard not to take the printed "volume one" as anything but a threat, but it is a kindly one under the care of a good reader. Spitzer's short rocket-style blasts of the absurd, visceral, and tradition-baiting vulgarity makes for that kind of nostalgic reading many of us had as kids with the flashlight under the bed covers reading Mad Magazine. If you liked Spitzer's "Riding the Unit", you'll most definitely enjoy this more. In some ways, the irreal-ist quality of these shorts, wondrously masked by trademark obscenity, turns The Art of Fiction (1984) on its ear. Again, maybe.

There's simply not one bit of bathos in the whole lot, so hang on tight to your lawn furniture and have this book kicking around your cottage this summer.

title: Outstanding book on grief
text:
Out to Sea is the kind of book I wish I had had for my daughter when my own mother — her nana — died. Death is a hard concept, especially for young children. And memories are fleeting. It was less than a month later that my daughter said she couldn’t remember Nana’s voice. It’s been three years, and most of the memories are gone, but we still find Nana in my daughter’s smile, in our garden, in books and in our hearts.

Out to Sea explains all this in such a simple and profound way. Helen Kellock’s sparse text and encompassing illustrations speak right to child’s — or adult’s — heart. And while exploring social and emotional issues, Kellock’s use of color and movement is exceptional. I highly recommend this book for families going through the grieving process.

title: Missing a heartbeat.
text: Okay--so there's a heartbeat to fiction, any fiction, long or short.  Beat: Exposition.  Beat: Rising Action.  Beat: Climax.  Beat: Falling action.  And in good, thoughtful fiction the falling action revisits the exposition and something has changed about the characters or the circumstances of the conflict--hopefully in all three.  I enjoyed Micah--I did.  He wasn't my favorite character, and now I like him more, and since I intend to continue reading this seminal series, that's a good thing, because he's become a big part of it.  In a way, reading this work was sort of like getting to know a brother in law you thought was just set decoration and finding out he's got a good sense of humor or something.  The problem with the novella was, that Anita, our main character, didn't seem to come to this--or any--conclusion about this character by the end of the story.  I needed to see some sort of reflection about Micah, about her acceptance of him in her life, in her bed, and instead, we jumped out of a (admittedly hot and character, uhm, building) sex scene, and into the metaphysics and although both parts were fun, there was no emotionally satisfying wrap up.  At the end, it was just Micah and Nathaniel and that's it, folks-- he's just set decoration again when we'd really started to think of him as a friend.  I still love this series, and I still like these characters, but this smaller installment was missing something vital.  It was missing a heartbeat.
